content: The test image shows a corn ear cross-section with white cottony mold at the center, with tan/brown discolored kernels. This narrows candidates to ear rot diseases. Let me examine the relevant reference images.

Based on my analysis:

**Test image observations:**
- Cross-section of a corn ear viewed from the tip
- Dense white cottony mold concentrated at the center
- Kernels appear tan/brown, discolored, some shrunken
- No pink/red coloration (rules out Gibberella)
- No green coloration (rules out Trichoderma, Aspergillus)
- No olive/yellow-green powdery spores (rules out Aspergillus)

**Comparison with candidates:**
- **Fusarium**: White to pink/salmon cottony mold on clustered kernels, with tan/brown discolored kernels — matches closely
- **Diplodia**: White mold starting at BASE of ear, grayish-brown uniform coverage — this cross-section appears to be from the tip, not base
- **Gibberella**: Pink-red mold at tip — no pink coloration present

The white cottony mold at the ear tip region with tan/brown kernels is most consistent with **Fusarium ear rot**. The Fusarium reference shows matching white cottony mold on kernels with similar tan/brown discoloration pattern.
